title: Benefit Charges on Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts: Reserve Postings and Reimbursement Bills
content:
Benefit charges recorded on an employer's charge positions under Employer Benefit Charging reach the employer's account in the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts once per quarter. A quarter's charges are the benefit charges posted on the charge positions of this employer account, less the charge credits reversed on them, counted by posting date within the calendar quarter.

## By financing method

| Employer | What happens to the quarter's charges | Amount due |
|---|---|---|
| Contributory | Posted against the reserve account, which lowers the reserve ratio at the next computation date | Nothing is created as due |
| Reimbursing | Billed as the same quarterly amount, due within the bill due days after mailing | The bill; interest runs on an unpaid bill as on unpaid contributions |

## Once per quarter

Charges of a quarter are posted or billed once per quarter, and a credit arising after posting reduces the next quarter's posting or bill. A quarter that already carries a posting or a bill on the account receives no second one.

**Hypothetical quarter.** Benefit charges of USD 3,200.00 are posted on the employer's charge positions in a quarter and USD 400.00 of charge credits are reversed on them in the same quarter, so the quarter's charges are USD 2,800.00.
- A contributory employer has USD 2,800.00 posted against its reserve account and owes nothing for it.
- A reimbursing employer is billed USD 2,800.00. With 30 bill due days and a bill mailed on 15 May, payment is due within the 30 calendar days after mailing, that is by 14 June.
- A credit of USD 150.00 arising after that posting reduces the next quarter's posting or bill by USD 150.00.
